quote_text:
Did that feel like a defeat? Yeah, I mean obviously to lose the equalizer  
in the 91st minute like we did, having defended  the box so well all afternoon, is frustrating.
In terms of cross balls coming in, I thought  the two center-backs were outstanding.
Just on that occasion, unfortunately,  
we couldn't get first contact, and then we  were out of position in the back post area.
So look, I can't have too many  complaints about the final score.
I thought Aberdeen were  excellent in the second half.
You can see with the changes they  made—the strength and depth that  
they've got within the squad,  real quality players coming on.
Jimmy Thelin had to gamble at halftime being  two goals down, and they put a lot of attacking  
players on the pitch, a lot of pace, and  good creativity with Clarkson as well.
For the majority of the half, we coped with it,  
we defended well, but unfortunately, we  just couldn't see it through to the end.
What changed then? Because, like you say, you  were very comfortable for most of the game. 
I think in the first half, we were really good.
I thought the high press was working,  we were able to get up the pitch,  
and in those transitions, we were really positive.
In the turnovers, we had quick counterattacks,  
got into some good areas, and scored two really  good goals off two well-worked set plays.
Obviously, we were delighted  at halftime to be in front.
But three games in a week is a really tough  ask for this particular group of players.
Given how low we are in numbers—we  were a man light in the squad today.
We've got key players like Will Ferry,  Ross Docherty, and Louis Moult all missing.
We had to ask Craig Sibbald  to start the game for us,  
having been out for the best part of  four months with a serious injury.
We knew we'd only get an hour out of  Craig, and I think losing Grimshaw in  
the first half denied us the opportunity  to make another couple of subs later on.
But look, in normal circumstances, I think  a point away from home is always a good one.
But obviously, having got so close to taking  maximum points, it's a real disappointment.
You had that chance just before Aberdeen got their  
second—did you feel like that  was going to be the winner? 
Yes, I mean Kai has got a real knack for finding  himself in good areas when the ball is out wide.
More often than not, I would expect  him to at least hit the target.
Disappointing finish, but we need to  defend the second goal a whole lot better.
Even the first one—I thought we were  far too open in the middle of the pitch.
But look, I can't be too critical of the players.
Three games in a week is a tough ask.
I think in the second half, particularly in the  
last 20-25 minutes, we just looked  like we ran out of a bit of energy.
Credit to Jimmy Thelin—the positive  changes he made at halftime paid off.
I think the least they deserved was a point on  the day, and we’ll go again in the next one.
What’s the situation with Grimshaw? Yeah, I mean, it’s around his pelvic  
area, maybe his groin.
It’s too early right now to give  a definitive answer on what it is,  
but that’ll be assessed on the  bus on the way back down the road.
We’ll have a better understanding of  what it looks like come tomorrow morning.
You mentioned injuries—how close are you  
to getting players back? It would be great to have them all back available.
For me, Will Ferry has probably been one  of our most consistent players all season.
I’ve got to give a lot of credit to Luke  Robinson—he's been an important player for  
us this season in pretty much  every position he’s played.
It’s not easy to go and play left-back,  especially against the pace and creativity  
that Aberdeen have got, so I think  he deserves a special mention.
But we hope to have Will and potentially  Louis Moult back in the squad.
Ross Docherty as well—we’ll  see how that progresses.
On the offside goal  decision—was it the right call? 
Yeah, I mean, that one probably  looked tight at the time.
But when I saw it back on the iPad on the dugout,  
I felt his left shoulder was just  slightly ahead of the Aberdeen backline.
So, gladly, we’re not talking about a  VAR decision that’s gone against us.
I think on this occasion, the  guys in VAR got that one right.
Finally, how important was it to have Craig  Sibbald back and come through this one unscathed? 
Yeah, of course, he’s a really  important player for us.
He was our player of the year last  season and has been out for four months.
He’s probably only had half a dozen  training sessions since returning to  
training—not anywhere near fit  enough to start the game today.
Our intention was always to gradually  build him up—give him 20 minutes,  
then half an hour, and then, hopefully  in a couple of weeks, start him.
But we had to throw him in early today given the  circumstances, and I thought he was fantastic.
It was a real good effort from the team.
It wasn’t a lack of fight or determination—I  just felt that we ran out of steam.
Aberdeen made really positive changes with a  lot of energy and pace, and they pinned us back.
Had we taken all three points,  obviously, we’d all be delighted.
Would I be sitting here saying  we deserved it? Probably not.
But it’s another point on the board for  us in terms of what our main objective is.
I think we need to try and  put a positive spin on it.
Although getting so close to taking all  three points is a major kick in the teeth.
Did you identify crosses as a possible  weakness in the Aberdeen defense? 
Yeah, look, we work hard on set  plays in the buildup to every game.
Similarly, the one on Wednesday night was a free  
kick that we had worked on—we  tried to isolate Sam Dalby.
We scored a legitimate goal on Wednesday,  
and unfortunately, it was chalked  off for all the wrong reasons.
Today, we identified that back area of Aberdeen.
We tried to get a couple of blockers in  there to try and isolate Richard Jensen.
The delivery from Glenn Middleton was outstanding.
You can do all the movement you want in the box,  
but if the delivery isn’t  good, then nothing else works.
It was a fantastic ball in  from Glenn, great header.
And the second one was again  something we worked on yesterday.
Fantastic delivery from Trpovski.
Aberdeen tend to send just one  player out to defend the corner,  
so we had that 2v1 situation where  we felt we had the advantage.
It was a great ball in from Trpovski  and another brilliant header from Dalby.
On Vik Stjepanovic’s impact I thought Vik was one that’s  
probably worthy of special mention.
He’s come from abroad, never played at this kind  of intensity before, and he’s been so at home.
For me, having played that position myself,  he’s probably been my player of the year so far.
Of course, Sam Dalby will get all the  headlines because center-forwards do  
the hardest job in the game—putting  the ball in the back of the net.
But Vik does so much unselfish work for the team.
I think he’s been a brilliant signing—really  shrewd business for us in the summer.
The way he trains day to day, his performances  on a Saturday, he’s a real team player.
Yeah, he’s been outstanding, and I  think we’re very fortunate to have him.
Is the key now to keep  supplying Dalby with chances? 
Yeah, well, we just need to continue putting  the ball into the right areas for them.
Because you’d back him in the air against anybody.
He’s been in terrific form, and this has  been a fantastic loan move for all parties.
If we can help him finish the  season as the top goal scorer,  
that would be a hell of an  achievement for him individually.
Thank you. Thanks.
title: "We ran out of steam" Jim Goodwin Post Match Press Conference | Aberdeen 2-2 Dundee United
